rulingTitle:
The script-opening scan tokenizes style contents as ordinary HTML, allowing tag-shaped CSS text to hide a subsequent script opening. For example, `

visible

` previously returned only `visible` with no links; the fix exposes the script comment and collects `https://hidden.example/`. The fake div's quoted attribute consumes the real script opening during the new tokenizer walk.

action.reason: Hold: the current code violates US-004's requirement to discard script and style contents. The script-removal pass scans style contents with the ordinary quote-aware tokenizer, so the supplied CSS fragment hides the subsequent script opening. Removing style afterward leaves script text and its link available for rendering and collection. This is not safe to waive: collected links become approval-relevant seen URLs.

rationale: Verified in html-text.ts: HIDDEN_TAGS processes script before style; dropRawText advances through nextTag without skipping other raw-text elements. readTag therefore allows the fake div's quoted attribute inside style to consume the real script opening. The spec explicitly requires both elements' contents to be removed; it provides no exception for this case.
